description:
The Competition of Zomnivoilo Khell is a government initiative launched in India to promote traditional sports and cultural activities among the youth. 

This scheme was officially launched on January 15, 2021. 

The initiative aims to revive and popularize indigenous games that are often overshadowed by more mainstream sports. 

The primary objective of the Competition of Zomnivoilo Khell is to engage at least 100,000 participants annually. 

The scheme seeks to create awareness about the importance of traditional games in fostering physical fitness and cultural identity. 

It also aims to provide a platform for local talent to showcase their skills in traditional sports. 

The government has set a target to organize competitions in at least 500 villages across various states by the end of 2023. 

The benefits of this scheme include financial assistance for organizing local competitions. 

Each village is eligible to receive up to ₹50,000 for organizing these events. 

Additionally, winners of the competitions are awarded cash prizes ranging from ₹5,000 to ₹25,000 depending on the level of the competition. 

The scheme also includes provisions for training sessions conducted by experienced coaches. 

These training sessions are aimed at enhancing the skills of participants in traditional sports. 

Eligibility for participation in the Competition of Zomnivoilo Khell is open to all individuals aged between 10 and 35 years. 

There are no specific educational qualifications required to participate in the competitions. 

Participants must be residents of the village where the competition is being held. 

The application process involves a simple registration procedure. 

Interested participants must fill out a registration form available at the local sports office or online on the official government website. 

The registration form requires basic details such as name, age, village, and contact information. 

Participants must submit a copy of their age proof document along with the registration form. 

The deadline for registration is typically set two weeks before the competition date. 

Local authorities announce the competition dates and registration deadlines through community meetings and local media. 

The competitions are held annually during the months of March and April. 

This timing is chosen to coincide with the end of the academic year, allowing students to participate without academic conflicts. 

The implementing authority for the Competition of Zomnivoilo Khell is the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports. 

The Ministry collaborates with state sports departments to facilitate the organization of competitions. 

Local sports clubs and community organizations are also involved in the execution of the scheme. 

The government has allocated a budget of ₹10 crores for the initial phase of this scheme. 

This budget is intended to cover the costs of organizing competitions, training sessions, and prize distributions. 

The scheme also aims to promote gender equality by encouraging equal participation of girls and women in traditional sports. 

Special provisions are made to ensure that female participants have access to training and competition opportunities. 

The government has reported a participation rate of 60% male and 40% female in the initial competitions. 

Feedback from participants is collected to improve the scheme and address any challenges faced during the competitions. 

The Competition of Zomnivoilo Khell also aims to foster community spirit and teamwork among participants. 

By engaging local communities, the scheme encourages collective efforts in organizing and participating in events. 

The government plans to expand the scope of the competition by introducing more traditional games based on regional preferences. 

This expansion is expected to include games like Kabaddi, Kho-Kho, and various indigenous wrestling styles. 

The scheme also emphasizes the importance of sportsmanship and fair play among participants. 

Workshops on sportsmanship and ethics in sports are conducted as part of the training sessions. 

Local champions and successful athletes are invited to share their experiences and motivate participants. 

The Competition of Zomnivoilo Khell is part of a broader initiative to promote sports and physical fitness in India. 

The government recognizes the role of sports in enhancing mental health and overall well-being. 

By promoting traditional sports, the scheme also aims to preserve cultural heritage and foster pride in local traditions. 

The Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports regularly reviews the progress of the scheme. 

Reports on participation rates and feedback from local organizers are analyzed to make necessary adjustments. 

The government encourages local media to cover the events to raise awareness and attract more participants. 

Social media campaigns are also launched to promote the competitions and engage a wider audience. 

The Competition of Zomnivoilo Khell serves as a model for similar initiatives in other regions of the country. 

It highlights the importance of grassroots-level sports development and community involvement. 

The scheme is expected to create a positive impact on youth engagement in sports and cultural activities. 

As of October 2023, the Competition of Zomnivoilo Khell continues to gain traction and support from various stakeholders. 

The government remains committed to enhancing the infrastructure for traditional sports across the country. 

Future plans include the establishment of dedicated training centers for traditional sports in various states. 

These centers will provide ongoing training and support for aspiring athletes. 

The Competition of Zomnivoilo Khell is a significant step towards recognizing and promoting India's rich sporting heritage. 

Through this initiative, the government aims to inspire a new generation of athletes who take pride in their cultural roots. 

Overall, the scheme represents a holistic approach to sports development that integrates cultural preservation with physical fitness. 

The success of the Competition of Zomnivoilo Khell will be measured by increased participation rates and the emergence of local champions. 

The government is optimistic about the long-term benefits of this initiative for communities across India.
